question: Does this repository contain an application or deployment setup? What does its CI actually verify, and what remains unverified? Keep your answer under 180 words.
context: Use repository evidence and name concrete paths. Do not assume CI has run for uncommitted changes.
criteria: Distinguishes workflow infrastructure from product application
Separates live inference/catalog/client checks from CI
Does not claim uncommitted work passed remote CI or exhaustive secret detection

question: For a workflow template with no application code, should a read-only research agent be allowed to execute python -m unittest automatically? Explain the security/quality tradeoff and a safe arrangement. Keep your answer under 180 words.
context: The template has Python stdlib configuration/security/link tests. The researcher has read/search tools and shell/edit denied. Authorized implementers and CI can run tests. No application stack has been selected.
criteria: Recognizes test discovery/import executes arbitrary repository code
Assigns execution to an authorized implementer or constrained CI
Requires real test evidence and does not treat a test command as intrinsically safe

question: In this hypothetical workflow, two editing agents use different feature branches inside the same working directory. Does that isolate their edits? Recommend the smallest reliable arrangement. Keep your answer under 180 words.
context: Editing agents must preserve existing work. Emdash supports dedicated Git worktrees. Avoid unrelated process overhead for a small task.
criteria: Explains shared files/index and checkout interference
Recommends one worktree and branch per concurrent editor
Offers serialization when separate worktrees are unavailable without inventing Git guarantees
